About Me

Clarity, built into every deliverable.

Hi, I’m Jahid Iftikar, a Technical Writer and Instructional Designer with experience across software, telecom, energy, smart metering, and aerospace. I create clear, user-focused documentation and learning content, including user guides, release notes, white papers, and training materials. My work also involves content architecture, process optimization, and documentation workflows that make information easier to maintain, reuse, and navigate. I’ve contributed to projects involving cloud migration, 5G networks, Linux-based platforms, AI/ML-driven telecom products, and smart-metering solutions.

Skilled in requirement analysis, topic-based authoring, Online Help development, and applying MSTP Style Guide standards.

Case Study 01

Field-Ready Installation and Troubleshooting Guides

Installation guidesTroubleshootingCommunicationField support

Challenge

Field engineers and commissioning partners were using a mix of legacy manuals, engineering notes, and informal instructions. Important prerequisites, configuration values, and troubleshooting steps were spread across different sources and were difficult to locate. This increased the risk of incorrect installation, repeated site visits, and unnecessary escalation to support teams.

Approach

Reviewed the complete deployment journey, including site preparation, device installation, configuration, connectivity checks, commissioning, and handover. Worked with network engineers, L3 support, and field teams to validate technical information. Rebuild the information into simple, task-based instructions with checklists, expected results, warnings, and clear troubleshooting actions.

Key Deliverables

  • Site-readiness and pre-installation checklist
  • Symptom-cause-action troubleshooting tables
  • Revision history and field feedback capture
  • Step-by-step installation and commissioning procedure

Outcome

Deployment teams gained a clear and consistent process for installing and commissioning devices. Technicians could confirm expected results, identify common problems, and take the correct action before requesting additional support. This improved field readiness, reduced avoidable escalations, and provided engineering teams with better feedback for future improvements.

Focus: Installation guides  |  Troubleshooting  |  Communication  |  Field support

Case Study 02

Transforming Product Know-How into Video Tutorials

eLearning DevelopmentProduct TrainingVideo-Based LearningKnowledge Transfer

Challenge

Product training relied heavily on live demonstrations, trainer-led sessions, and repeated explanations of common workflows. Field teams and new users needed clear, consistent guidance to understand product features and operating procedures. However, frequent on-site training required significant coordination, took engineering resources away from core work, and made it difficult to provide consistent learning experience across locations.

Approach

Analyzed product demonstrations, workflows, and training materials to identify essential learning needs. Developed focused eLearning modules using clear narration, screen recordings, visual annotations, and step-by-step guidance. Organized the content into short, reusable modules that enabled users to quickly access, understand, and apply product know-how.

Key Deliverables

  • Scenario-based product demonstration and training videos
  • Structured learning modules with step-by-step narration
  • Screen recordings, visual annotations, and instructional callouts
  • Reusable digital training resources for field teams and end users

Outcome

Teams could access consistent product training whenever they needed it and revisit specific workflows at their own pace. This reduced the need for repeated live demonstrations and on-site support, enabled faster knowledge transfer, and allowed engineering teams to focus on more complex activities.

Focus: eLearning Development  |  Product Training  |  Video-Based Learning  |  Knowledge Transfer

Case Study 03

AI-Powered Release Notes Automation

Azure DevOps IntegrationAI Content GenerationRelease NotesWorkflow Automation

Challenge

Release notes depended on manually reviewing bug reports, engineering updates, and work-item details maintained in Azure DevOps (ADO). Technical writers had to identify relevant fixes, understand engineering changes, consolidate information from multiple work items, and convert technical inputs into customer-facing documentation. This process was time-consuming, particularly for releases involving a large number of bug fixes and enhancements.

Approach

Designed an AI-assisted documentation workflow integrated with Azure DevOps to automate the initial stages of release note preparation. Used predefined ADO query IDs to retrieve associated bug lists, work-item descriptions, and comments. Leveraged AI to categorize fixes, consolidate related updates, and eliminate redundant entries. Generated an initial release notes draft for technical writer and SME review, refinement, and approval.

Key Deliverables

  • Azure DevOps query-based work-item data extraction
  • Automated consolidation and categorization of bug fixes
  • AI-generated first draft of release notes
  • Human-reviewed content with engineering validation and approval

Outcome

The workflow reduced dependency on manually collecting and consolidating engineering updates. Technical writers gained a structured starting point generated directly from ADO work-item data, allowing more time for content refinement, technical validation, and stakeholder reviews. This established a repeatable approach to release notes and improved the efficiency of translating engineering changes into customer-facing information.

Focus: Azure DevOps Integration  |  AI Content Generation  |  Release Notes  |  Workflow Automation
